comparator.name: Public Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 OER Appendix3 p31 and the official year pages agree on one 180-EC framework: 60EC compulsory first year; 48EC compulsory second year plus12EC from four listed restricted options; and18EC compulsory advanced study,30EC genuine free choice in third-year semester1 and a12EC thesis. Retain the first two restricted options in the published list, Security in the Netherlands and Challenges in Policy Advising, selected neutrally before UCR matching and subject to capacity. No named route is required. Appendix4 pp32–33 explicitly accepts current replacements for the older methods prerequisites: thesis entry is90EC including Academic Skills, Public Administration Research Methodology and Applied Quantitative Methods. This sequence satisfies the conditions. European Governance excludes MAN-BCU348A, which is not selected. Free-space choices require approval/non-overlap; internships can be6,12or18EC and require90EC including the full first year. Mandatory academic Dutch language testing carries no additional credits. BSA normally42of60EC; attendance, interim work and proposal conditions apply as recorded in component notes. Appendix4 repeats BPRA201 next to quantitative methods, but Appendix3 and the current year-page course link unambiguously identify the separate quantitative unit as BPRA200; no unit or credit is duplicated. This is the current published framework; future offerings may change.

core: Public policy, government institutions and the governance of societal problems
Public organisations, citizens, law, politics, economics and public values
Policy formation, implementation, evaluation and evidence-based problem solving
Quantitative, qualitative and independent research into policy and governance
Policy advice, communication and democratic engagement
adjacent: Public organisations, leadership and digital governance
questions: Why do some policies work while others fail, and how can public problems be addressed?
How can governments respond to climate change and sustainability transitions?
How can public organisations be governed, led and adapted in a digital age?

trace: Complementary digital-governance perspective: business cases analyse AI, innovation, labour, privacy, bias, fairness, corporate governance and regulation. These tools inform organisational choices; the course does not reproduce digital public services or the full e-government syllabus.
introduces economic reasoning about markets, institutions and government choices
examines macroeconomic conditions and policy in an international setting
analyses incentives and behavioural mechanisms shaping individual and policy outcomes
examines market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation and public intervention
provides econometric methods for evaluating relationships and policy-relevant evidence

Complementary social-innovation practice: teams develop a new venture, business model, market validation and pitch, including social entrepreneurship. This is a specific organisational innovation tool, not general public-administration theory.
provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis
develops ethical leadership communication and persuasive practice
examines inclusive leadership and diversity management in organisations
examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures
develops negotiation, strategic interaction and decision-making under competing interests
Complementary empirical tools: cleaning, manipulating and visualising tabular, spatial and text data, with a research project across disciplines. Public-policy datasets are not guaranteed.
directly studies institutions, participation and policy for sustainability transitions
Complementary environmental framework: planetary boundaries identify the environmental limits within which policy and governance choices are made; this is not public administration training.

Direct thematic grounding for climate policy: scientific drivers, environmental and societal impacts, adaptation, mitigation, interest-group misinformation, climate governance and justice are studied together.
Complementary assessment method: life-cycle impacts of products, processes and services and circular-economy planning inform environmental policy trade-offs. This is not a policy-process course.

Complementary applied sustainability research: small teams study a question supplied by a regional institution or company with external advice. The topic is not necessarily public policy, and the project is not a separate individual bachelor thesis.
examines how law structures social relations, institutions and justice
compares constitutional institutions, public authority and democratic arrangements
examines EU institutions, legal authority and multilevel governance

Complementary normative method: moral theories, responsibility, equality, wealth, future generations and climate support judgments about public choices. This is general ethics rather than a dedicated administrative-ethics syllabus.
provides comparative analysis of political institutions, regimes and government
examines EU institutions, decision-making and political governance

Complementary conflict-governance analysis: regional, national and international cases examine structural inequality, ideology, colonial grievances, institutions and civil-society peacebuilding. No Dutch public-safety organisation syllabus is claimed.
introduces social institutions, inequality and the analysis of societal problems
develops qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity

Complementary social theory: modernity, imperialism, colonial responses and debates in sociology contextualise public institutions and inequality. This is not a dedicated citizen–government relations course.
examines collective action, environmental justice and political mobilisation

Direct public-sphere and civil-society analysis: Gramsci, Habermas, Fraser, solidarity, civil repair and decolonial critiques frame an empirical NGO or civil-society organisation study. Government agencies are not guaranteed project subjects.

Complementary behavioural foundations: scientific social psychology examines how the presence of others shapes thought, feelings and behaviour; application to citizen behaviour is supplied by the programme.

Complementary academic and professional communication: rhetorical analysis, argument, writing and oral presentation support public and organisational communication; no dedicated policy-advice project is guaranteed.
examines how climate problems are framed and communicated to publics

Direct public-communication method: framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and persuasion ethics are applied in a local-institution communication project. This supports the communication dimension of advice, not the whole policy-advising process.

Direct public-law context: sources and institutions of public international law, state authority, treaties, compliance, refugee and environmental law support analysis of public organisations beyond the national state. This does not reproduce comparative public-administration practice.

alternatives.label: Public policy, governance & institutions
alternatives.concept: A broad route through public policy and governance, combining political and legal institutions, public economics, sociology, civil society, organisational psychology, European governance and quantitative and qualitative inquiry. Dedicated policy implementation, Dutch administration and a separate public-administration thesis remain specialist gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: A broad route through public policy and governance, combining political and legal institutions, public economics, sociology, civil society, organisational psychology, European governance and quantitative and qualitative inquiry. Dedicated policy implementation, Dutch administration and a separate public-administration thesis remain specialist gaps.
progression: Political, sociological, economic, research and legal foundations support advanced public economics, EU law and politics, organisational psychology, communication and econometrics. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every assigned offering passes; advisory sequencing is considered without inventing additional hard rules.
traceOverrides: develops data cleaning, visualisation and analysis for evidence-informed policy research
develops negotiation, strategic interaction and decision-making for policy processes
examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures in public and other organisations
examines leadership, inclusion and diversity within organisations

alternatives.label: Climate policy & sustainability governance
alternatives.concept: A climate-policy and sustainability-governance route centred on public institutions, law, public economics, participation, environmental justice, communication and empirical methods. Climate science, planetary boundaries and life-cycle assessment provide specific grounding for policy choices; regional sustainability research supplies applied practice without guaranteeing a policy topic.
alternatives.labelReason: A climate-policy and sustainability-governance route centred on public institutions, law, public economics, participation, environmental justice, communication and empirical methods. Climate science, planetary boundaries and life-cycle assessment provide specific grounding for policy choices; regional sustainability research supplies applied practice without guaranteeing a policy topic.
alternatives.distinctness: Climate policy is organised around environmental justice, public communication and sustainability governance, with targeted environmental methods and regional research. It differs from preceding alternatives by [8] courses respectively. These are curricular consequences of the concepts, not threshold-filling changes.
progression: Politics, climate, sustainability, research and law support later sustainability governance, environmental justice, public economics, social theory, EU study and applied regional research. Five technical or sector-science courses are replaced with ethics, data, AI governance, social theory and econometrics. Every formal prerequisite and assigned offering is checked against the workbook.

alternatives.label: Public organisations, leadership & digital governance
alternatives.concept: A route centred on public organisations, leadership and digital governance. Comparative politics, public international law, constitutional law, EU politics and civil society anchor organisational psychology, communication, quantitative and qualitative methods. AI governance and social-venture creation supply specific complementary tools for organisational change.
alternatives.labelReason: A route centred on public organisations, leadership and digital governance. Comparative politics, public international law, constitutional law, EU politics and civil society anchor organisational psychology, communication, quantitative and qualitative methods. AI governance and social-venture creation supply specific complementary tools for organisational change.
alternatives.distinctness: Public organisations are organised around leadership communication, rhetorical practice, AI governance, social innovation and public international law, replacing part of the broad route’s macro/public economics, general sociology, conflict and EU-law emphasis. It differs from preceding alternatives by [5, 9] courses respectively. These are curricular consequences of the concepts, not threshold-filling changes.
progression: Comparative politics, social innovation, data, research, sociology, communication and law support public international law, organisational psychology, civil society, EU politics and econometrics. Three generic upper-level business courses are replaced with public law, civil-society study and microeconomics. All formal prerequisites and assigned offerings pass.

candidates.label: Public organisations, leadership and digital governance

selection.assessment: Three evidence-backed related routes respond to the defining public problem, policy, institution and organisational substance. General coherence or environmental/business labels alone do not establish comparability under the CP119 distinction. Five science/engineering placements in the climate route and three generic business placements in the organisations route are replaced with stronger public, social and empirical study. Housing and poverty remain evidenced public problems; the separate candidate lacks a sustained available housing-policy sequence beyond general economics and sociology, so it is not included under a new label. Public Policy Analysis exists in the workbook but is unavailable in the planned semesters and cannot fill that gap. Pairwise course differences are [{'pair': [1, 2], 'differentCourses': 8}, {'pair': [1, 3], 'differentCourses': 5}, {'pair': [2, 3], 'differentCourses': 9}]. The maximum of three is reached only after these substantive tests.

notes.text: These UCR routes offer substantial political, legal, economic, social and organisational analysis with empirical methods. Radboud provides a dedicated public-administration sequence in policy formation and implementation, Dutch administration, public-sector practice, digital government and a separate 12-EC thesis. UCR does not reproduce every specialist unit; optional independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-taught Public Administration degree studies how policy, government and public organisations shape societal problems, and how their effects can be understood and improved. It combines political, legal, economic and social perspectives with empirical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR routes offer related study in public policy and institutions, climate governance, or public organisations and digital change. Radboud adds a dedicated public-administration sequence, Dutch policy practice and a separate bachelor thesis. The UCR routes develop related academic capacities and do not confer the same disciplinary qualification.
